statement: enforcer-validator depends on enforcer-rules (not the reverse), so a literal `impl Validator` for a rule owned by enforcer-rules cannot live inside enforcer-rules itself -- that would be a circular crate dependency. The d13 workpack's 'T1 Validator in enforcer-rules' phrasing describes the concept, not a literal trait impl location. The correct shape (confirmed by the TEST_PROOF_EXPECTATIONS.md d13 proof row, which pins the command to `cargo test -p enforcer-rules` with no dependency on enforcer-validator): a pure check function returning enforcer_domain::findings::Finding directly from enforcer-rules, since enforcer-rules already depends on enforcer-domain.
why: Any future workpack whose acceptance block says 'a Validator in <data-crate>' where <data-crate> is downstream of enforcer-validator will hit this same circular-dependency wall; the fix is always 'emit Findings directly, let a higher layer wrap it as a Validator if it ever needs to', not editing Cargo.toml to force the dependency backwards.
howToApply: Before adding any `impl Validator` inside a *-rules/*-domain/*-config style data crate, check `cargo tree -p enforcer-validator -i <your-crate>` (or just read enforcer-validator's Cargo.toml) -- if your crate is a dependency of enforcer-validator, you cannot implement its Validator trait locally.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-validator/Cargo.toml depends on enforcer-rules; crates/enforcer-rules/Cargo.toml has no enforcer-validator dependency

statement: clippy::expect_used (workspace deny-wall) rejects `.expect(...)` even on a provably-unreachable branch (e.g. re-parsing enforcer_core::hash_chain::link_digest's own output back through Sha256::try_from, which cannot fail given link_digest's documented output shape). The established idiom elsewhere in this workspace for a genuinely-impossible branch is `unreachable!("reason")`, NOT `.expect("reason")` -- clippy::panic (also denied) only catches explicit `panic!()` calls, it does not flag the `unreachable!` macro. enforcer_core::hash_chain's own test suite already uses this exact pattern (`Ok(_) => unreachable!("tampered chain must not verify")`).
why: Every future 'this branch cannot happen, but the type system requires a match arm' situation in this workspace should reach for `unreachable!(msg)`, not `.expect(msg)` or `.unwrap()` -- the first candidate someone reaches for (expect with a good message) is exactly the one the deny-wall blocks.
howToApply: When a Result/Option branch is provably unreachable by an upstream invariant, write `match value { Ok(x) => x, Err(_) => unreachable!("why this cannot happen") }` instead of `.expect("why this cannot happen")`.

evidence.ref: cargo clippy -p enforcer-rules --all-targets -- -D warnings; error: used `expect()` on a `Result` value at version_drift.rs:221 before fix, clean after switching to unreachable!()

statement: When modeling a 4-shape drift comparison (unchanged / bumped-cleanly / content-changed-no-bump / hollow-bump) as a match over two booleans derived from a > comparison (e.g. `version_bumped = candidate.version > baseline.version`), a version DECREASE silently collapses into the same boolean as 'no change' (both are `false`), making any enum variant meant to distinguish a decrease permanently unreachable dead code. Caught via manual review (not a test failure) in check_registry_drift's ManifestDrift::HashUnchangedVersionMismatch variant, which no test could ever construct until the comparison was rewritten as a three-way `.cmp()` (Ordering::Less/Equal/Greater) instead of a boolean `>`.
why: Any drift/ratchet/version-comparison oracle in this codebase that reduces a numeric comparison to a single boolean (>) rather than a three-way Ordering will have the same silent-decrease-is-invisible gap; worth grep-checking `d02`'s baseline_ratchet and similar ratchet mechanisms for the same pattern.
howToApply: When comparing a monotonic counter/version across baseline vs candidate for drift purposes, use `.cmp()` and match on Ordering::{Less,Equal,Greater} rather than a single `a > b` boolean, so a decrease is a distinct, nameable outcome instead of silently aliasing to 'unchanged'.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-rules/src/version_drift.rs check_registry_drift: added version_decrease_with_unchanged_content_fails_closed_against_manifest unit test to prove HashUnchangedVersionMismatch is now reachable

statement: rule-version-manifest.json (d13) pins only the 4 baseline catalogs (deny-wall/no-reexports/ocentra-parent-posture/deferred-work-gate, 7 rule ids) that tests/registry_load.rs's all_baseline_records() already assembles into arc-04's own proven whole-registry -- NOT all 32 files under crates/enforcer-rules/rules/**. There is no existing single aggregation point that loads every catalog into one registry (each family's own *_registry.rs integration test loads only its own catalog); building one for d13 alone would invent new owns-surface outside d13's `owns:` line and immediately go stale as sibling lanes (d16, d17, d22, ...) add rule records in parallel.
why: If a future workpack wants a manifest/drift-gate over the FULL rule catalog (all families), that is a new cross-cutting aggregation concern -- likely its own workpack -- not a silent scope-creep add-on to d13's disjoint-owns.
howToApply: Before widening rule-version-manifest.json's coverage, first check whether a canonical all-catalogs RuleRegistry assembly point exists yet (grep for a function that includes every rules/*.json file, not just one family's own test). If none exists, that assembly point is its own workpack, not a drive-by addition here.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-rules/src/rules/mod.rs has no all() aggregator; only per-family *_registry.rs test files each load their own catalog independently
